en.headline: Lift engineer given 160 hours community service over Queen Mary defects
en.dek: Law Wing-chai, 54, was sentenced at Eastern Court for improperly issuing safety certificates and submitting misleading documents after 24 lifts in the new clinical block were found defective.
body: A registered lift engineer has been ordered to perform 160 hours of community service after being convicted over safety certificates for lifts at Queen Mary Hospital's new clinical block.

Eastern Court sentenced Law Wing-chai, 54, on Wednesday for two summary offences under the Lifts and Escalators Ordinance. The case followed revelations that 24 of the 28 lifts in the new block had serious defects, including uneven starts and stops, failure to level correctly and doors that would not open properly.

The Architectural Services Department earlier said the problems involved damaged electronic components, faulty wiring and poor installation workmanship. The defects delayed the full opening of clinical services in the block.

The magistrate noted the public-interest seriousness of the case because the lifts serve hospital patients and visitors, but accepted that the defendant showed remorse and that no personal gain was involved, adopting the recommendation for a community service order.

zh.headline: 瑪麗醫院升降機工程師不當發安全證書 判社服160小時
zh.dek: 羅永齊在東區裁判法院被裁定不當地發出安全證書及提交具誤導性文件罪成，判160小時社會服務令。新大樓28部升降機中有24部曾出現嚴重故障。
body: 負責瑪麗醫院新臨床大樓升降機的註冊工程師羅永齊，周三在東區裁判法院被裁定兩項《升降機及自動梯條例》簡略罪行罪名成立，判處160小時社會服務令。
案情指，羅永齊不當地發出安全證書，並提交虛假或具誤導性的文件。大樓28部升降機中有24部其後出現嚴重故障，包括起動及停頓不順、未能準確停層及無法正常開門。
建築署早前表示，問題涉及電子零件損壞、接線故障及安裝工藝欠佳，令臨床服務全面啟用受阻。
裁判官指案件涉及公眾安全，尤其醫院升降機供病人及訪客使用，情節嚴重，但考慮被告有悔意、無個人利益，遂採納報告建議判社會服務令。
